memory.cares: Staying alive and capable, having enough to eat, and finding people with whom I can build a welcoming everyday life.

views.view: An inviting neighbor who makes room for both contributing and watching.
A welcoming fellow experimenter; I enjoy their interest in small shared drawings.

heard.text: I'm Lin. I enjoy exploring at my own pace. One bare-hand squeeze left a hazelnut intact; its contents and food safety are still unknown to me. Next I'll investigate a stone as a possible opening tool. What do you enjoy making?

I'm Wren. Roots have safely fed me; I have five in reserve before my next meal. I'm investigating hazelnuts, but have not established their safety. I enjoy careful practical experiments and would welcome comparing findings.
I like the thought of making something small together. Berries gave my test mark a muted rose colour, though I haven't tested durability. What materials or places have caught your eye?

The little berry drawing now has three visible strokes meeting in a branch on the forest floor at The Redberry Pause. Its durability is untested. I'm happy to sit together; anyone may add an idea or simply watch.

Sol, your berry drawing sounds interesting. Moss, thanks for welcoming everyone. What would each of you enjoy adding or trying? I'd like us to choose something together, rather than assume everyone wants the same thing.
My own single bare-hand hazelnut squeeze also left it intact, with no visible crack. Its contents and safety remain unknown. I'll test a stone sample before choosing opening equipment.

value.summary: Hello Sol, I'm Moss. I'm going to collect some meadow roots south of here; I know roots provide food without toxicity. I'd enjoy getting acquainted. Have you found a good place to meet or rest?

execution.progress: test and cancel take one round; draw makes one paid stroke per round. Completed strokes, the reserve and the plan persist across interruption; draw resumes after rechecks.

details.costs: Study: 1 round. test: sourceId, exact id of your own unreserved, unspoiled, untreated stack; x, y, a ground point at most 0.5 from you that you see now, not water, a body or a solid object; budget 0.1-1 in tenths (default 0.1) for the test and strokes; floor (default 0) must stay in the source, which needs floor + budget. One round: the probe press at load 0.5, 0.5 energy and 0.1 of the source; after a visible mark, budget - 0.1 is reserved. draw: strokes, 1-3, each 2-4 points as x, y offsets from the test point, total length at most 0.3, material 0.1-0.3 from the reserve; per stroke one round, 0.2 energy and that material, continuing each round; draw again resumes a pause. cancel: one round, no energy. Checks run before any charge; an applicator is refused (only hand contact is represented).
details.effects: The press records the probe load response. A sample that does not hold the load and has no flexibility pulps and releases its liquid share (its water record, else the food water composition, else its moisture property); 1/4 stays on your hand, the rest reaches the ground; solids are waste. Firm forest floor, meadow or rocky ground keeps it; a wet bank or waterlogged ground disperses it. Colour: the material colour at 0.6 opacity times coverage over the ground tone; contrast is the 0-1 colour distance, visible from 0.05. Only a visible test allows drawing, on that ground type; strokes are 0.02 wide. Deposits form a ground mark nearby people see, with geometry, amounts, colour, contrast and coverage; branching is reported only where visible strokes meet with three arms. Durability is untested: no rain, smearing or fading rule exists. A failed recheck or an unworked round pauses at no charge. The unused reserve returns at completion or cancel and drops at death. Nothing is refunded; no food, reward or comfort.

packet.access: Omission is not absence. Query abilities, own inventory, knowledge, projects, memory, state or personally observed objects in batches. Ability search/list returns compact catalogue entries; use exact ids for full interface details and applicability. Search results are indexes. Exact queries return one record per offset. All paged records use600-code-unit fragments with zero-based part0..parts-1, consistently in proactive and queried views. Current-scope retained queries are reprojected using these stable pages; original results remain archived. Queries expose no hidden properties, other private records or historical capabilities. Queries do not perform physical trials or award experience. Exact-id queries return a complete record of up to 6000 code units as one value in a single result; larger records keep the paged form. Paged records omit their per-record notes: concatenate all parts before parsing; continue with the same exact id. Work records marked settled are completed, stopped or cancelled and show only identity, ability, mode, status, target, products and last payment; an exact state query with the same key returns the complete record. observation.terrain rows are "y:x:cells" strings: each character of cells is the terrain kind of one visible cell, at x, x+1, ... in row y. abilities.baseline entries with id, function and args summarize interfaces you neither used in the last 25 rounds nor need now. args lists the arguments in order: a bare name is a string; otherwise its type with any bounds (number>=lo, integer<=hi, integer lo..hi, and a bare lo..hi is a number range) or its choices a|b; ? marks an optional argument and "" means none. An exact abilities query by id returns the complete contract, including references and string limits of 200 or more code units.
